symptom: `mxcli new` exits 1 at step 7 when the Linux devcontainer binary can't be downloaded, although the project is complete (always fails with a dev build)
cause: Step 7 (Windows/macOS: download the Linux mxcli for the devcontainer) called os.Exit(1) on any download error, after steps 1-6 had already produced a usable project; step 6 next to it already downgraded its own failure to a warning. Every dev build hit it: a plain `go build` leaves main.Version empty so the version is the 0.1.0 default and mxcliReleaseTag() asks for release v0.1.0, which is a guaranteed 404 (a tagless `make build` asks for v<commit-hash>)
insight: An exit code is a claim about the whole command, so a best-effort step late in a multi-step command must not own it — audit each step's failure branch against whether the artefact is already usable, not against how that step was written in isolation. The existing test even documented the bug as the spec ('must exit 1'). For a release lookup, decide from main.Version (the ldflags value), not from the resolved `version`, whose 0.1.0 default looks like a real semver and hides that no release can match. Testing an os.Exit is cheap: move the step into a helper that writes to io.Writers and call it from a test — the unfixed helper kills the test binary with exit 1 before any assertion, which is the reported symptom reproduced. E2E on Windows, same dev build both ways: unfixed `HTTP 404 ... v0.1.0`, exit=1, .mpr present; fixed exit=0; a v9.9.9 build (download 404s) warns and exits 0
